newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine call money rises on weekend borrowing.
newsitem.headline: Philippine call money rises on weekend borrowing.

text.p: * Interbank call average rises to 11.96875 pct
Philippine overnight money rose to 11.96875 percent on Monday from Friday's 11.09375 percent as banks scoured for short-term funds to cover their weekend reserve deficiencies, traders said.
"This is just the usual Monday tightness," one trader said. Trades in the interbank call market are valued the previous trading day.
Turnover was heavy with 24.028 billion pesos changing hands among 66 institutions, 41 of which were on the lending side.

One trader said the rate did not rise as sharply as had been feared, especially after last Friday's heavy dollar-selling by the Central Bank, as banks were told up to 36 billion pesos worth of government securities were due to mature in October.
"If there won't be any rate adjustments by Central Bank, we expect rates to decline," he added.
Another trader said interest rates would remain soft due to lower inflation rate. Most analysts expect inflation, due out on Friday, to be lower than August's 7.9 percent.
The optimism was carried over to the longer-termed securities.
Secondary rates of Treasury bills were hovering near last week's average rate. Traders were expecting the rates to remain steady in this afternoon's auction.
Three-month bills were being traded at 11.55 to 11.6 percent, six-month bills at 11.85 to 11.875 percent, and one-year bills at 12.6 to 12.7 percent.
